title: Partial Pre-Post Code Tree: A Memory-Efficient Tree Structure for Conjunctive Rule Mining

problem.claim: Large-scale conjunctive rule mining requires memory-efficient data structures for answering arbitrary conjunctive queries.

gap.claim: Full PPC-tree construction creates a memory bottleneck because PPC-trees are built as an intermediate representation before conversion to N-lists.

contributions.claim: Introduces partial pre-post code trees (P3C-trees), which iteratively construct partial trees and immediately convert them into N-lists.
Integrates tree construction and N-list conversion to avoid full PPC-tree memory consumption.
Uses P3C-trees to accelerate N-list construction.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments with big datasets report that P3C-trees use orders of magnitude less memory than PPC-trees.
The generated N-lists are reported to be more effective than Tidset and Diffset structures.
The P3C-tree structure is reported to considerably speed up N-list construction.

narrative_sequence.summary: Rule mining algorithms summarize training data in structures that support fast conjunctive queries.
The main limitation of these structures is memory consumption, particularly during full PPC-tree construction.
P3C-trees iteratively construct partial trees and immediately convert them into N-lists.
This integration targets memory scalability and is reported to reduce memory use, improve N-list effectiveness, and accelerate construction.

source_observation.claim: Immediate conversion of partial intermediate structures can avoid the memory cost of materializing a full tree.

interpretation.claim: Integrating staged construction with downstream representation conversion may reduce peak memory usage in data-mining pipelines.

application.claim: For large-scale mining systems, evaluate whether partial materialization and early conversion can replace full intermediate representations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach benefits datasets or workloads outside the reported experiments.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not describe the P3C-tree algorithm in implementation detail.
The abstract does not quantify the reported speedups or memory reductions beyond their qualitative magnitude.
